name: mixpanelyst
works_with: Claude Code, as part of the mixpanel-headless plugin. The underlying Python library and mp CLI run on Python 3.10+
short: Lets your coding agent answer Mixpanel questions by writing and running Python against your project's data.
what: An analysis skill from Mixpanel's own plugin. Ask about trends, funnels, retention, user paths, cohorts or experiments in plain language, and the agent writes Python with the mixpanel_headless library and pandas, runs it, and answers from the result. It also teaches the agent which defaults mislead, how to check a result, and how to manage entities like feature flags, alerts and Lexicon.
who: Product managers, analysts and engineers who already use Mixpanel and work in Claude Code. Skip it if you don't have Mixpanel data, or if you want to add tracking code to an app (the skill says it is not for that).
needs: Python 3.10 or later, or uv (setup builds a private Python environment with one of them)
A Mixpanel account: a service account, a browser login, or an OAuth token

steps.title: Run setup once
steps.text: It creates a private Python environment under ~/.claude/plugins/data/ and installs mixpanel_headless 0.4.0 or later there, never into your system Python.

steps.title: Connect your Mixpanel account
steps.text: The auth skill shows the session and lets you log in or switch accounts, projects and workspaces. The library's recommended first command is mp login, which opens a browser login by default.

try.label: From the README
try.text:
How many signups last week?

Then try:
Where do users drop off in checkout?
Do users come back after onboarding?

watch: When the skill runs, the plugin pre-approves its Python and mp commands for that turn, including ones that change or delete Mixpanel objects. The skills tell the agent to list objects and ask before any delete. Add ask or deny rules in your Claude Code permissions if you want a prompt for each command.
Credentials are saved to ~/.mp/config.toml. If you run mp login with MP_OAUTH_TOKEN set, the token is stored there inline.
Each report link the agent creates stores a new record in Mixpanel.
The library is pre-release. The README says APIs may change before 1.0.
